title: Anzick-1 (Clovis infant burial, Montana)
summary: Anzick-1 was a male infant aged approximately one to two years who was buried with red ochre and more than one hundred Clovis stone and bone tools at site 24PA506 in western Montana around 12,600 years ago. As the only known Clovis-associated human burial, his successfully sequenced genome demonstrated that ancient Clovis populations were directly ancestral to contemporary Native Americans, especially in Central and South America. Following respectful tribal consultations, his remains were reburied in 2014.

as_recorded.value: The child’s remains were reburied at the site in 2014, amid controversy centered on the need for tribal consultation

where.modern_name: Anzick site (24PA506), near Wilsall, Park County, Montana, United States
where.historical_name: Shields River Valley, beneath a rock ledge, southwestern Montana, North America

importance.justification: Anzick-1 is the only known human burial directly associated with the Clovis complex, and his sequenced genome definitively proved the Asian genetic origin and continuous ancestry of Native American populations.
